title: OpenAI Unveils GPT 5.6: A Powerful Leap in Agentic AI and Multimodal Capabilities
summary: OpenAI has launched GPT 5.6, its latest family of highly intelligent models comprising Soul, Terra, and Luna variants, designed for advanced agentic workflows and complex, multi-step tasks. Accessible via a redesigned ChatGPT desktop app (Codeex), the models demonstrate impressive capabilities in real-time web app creation, physics simulations, autonomous content generation, and deep research. While showcasing significant performance gains and cost-efficiency over competitors like Claude Fable in various benchmarks, GPT 5.6 exhibits some limitations in visual content accuracy and a higher hallucination rate on specific tests. This release underscores a strategic shift towards AI models capable of prolonged, autonomous work and emergent learning, accelerating internal R&D at OpenAI.
article:
OpenAI has officially released GPT 5.6, introducing a new generation of highly intelligent models engineered for complex, agentic workflows and demanding computational tasks. This latest family includes three distinct variants: GPT 5.6 Soul, the largest and most performant; Terra, a mid-range option; and Luna, the smallest and fastest model. While foundational AI capabilities like email drafting, summarization, and basic research are effortlessly managed, the true power of GPT 5.6 emerges when tackling intricate, multi-step challenges that push the boundaries of current AI.

To fully leverage GPT 5.6's capabilities, particularly for tasks involving multiple files, tools, or sequential steps, OpenAI emphasizes its integration with agentic frameworks. The redesigned Codeex application, now rebranded as the ChatGPT desktop app, serves as the primary interface. Available for various operating systems, this free desktop application allows users to deploy multiple agents concurrently, interacting with local files and folders. It also supports saving reusable skills and scheduling automations, providing a more robust environment than the online ChatGPT platform.

Demonstrating its advanced multimodal and agentic prowess, GPT 5.6 was put through a series of rigorous tests. One notable achievement involved generating a real-time, voice-interactive web application featuring an animated anime character. The model autonomously coded the entire application, integrated Google's Gemini real-time voice model for conversational interaction, and utilized GPT Image to generate multiple images for lip-sync animations. This complex task was completed in a single prompt, requiring no follow-up corrections, highlighting its end-to-end coding and integration capabilities.

In physics understanding, GPT 5.6 was tasked with simulating liquid splashes, complete with adjustable gravity and light settings, and controlled via webcam hand-tracking. Crucially, the model was instructed to code everything from scratch, eschewing external libraries with pre-rendered animations. It successfully delivered a visually accurate simulation with dynamic controls, again from a single prompt, underscoring its ability to generate complex, interactive physics models.

The model also showcased its capacity for autonomous tool use and content creation. When asked to produce a promotional video for ByteDance's Cdream 5 Pro image model, GPT 5.6 was provided only with the product page, a GitHub repository for the Hyperframes animation tool, and Gemini TTS documentation. It autonomously navigated the GitHub repo to install Hyperframes, used Gemini TTS for voiceover generation, and synthesized product images into a minute-long video. While the resulting video's visual aesthetics, such as text placement and spacing, still exhibited some imperfections, the model's ability to orchestrate multiple tools and information sources autonomously was remarkable.

Further tests included generating a Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) interface with a 32-bar expressive song, complete with piano roll editing, pan, volume, effects, and automation. After an initial "robotic" output, a follow-up prompt for "more variation and creativity" led to a significantly improved, coherent song with risers, drops, and orchestrated instruments, demonstrating its iterative refinement capabilities. In 3D scene rendering, GPT 5.6 attempted to reconstruct a complex animated scene from a single image. While it produced a coherent 3D environment with well-formed objects, it did not precisely replicate the reference image, indicating an area for further development. The model also successfully generated a complex Manim math animation of a butterfly using epicycles, autonomously installing the Manim tool and creating an intricate visual output.

However, GPT 5.6's performance in vision-specific tasks presented a mixed bag. When asked to identify tumor types in medical scans, it attempted to classify them but made several incorrect diagnoses, failing to identify all tumors and misidentifying some conditions. This contrasts with Claude Fable's tendency to refuse biology-related questions entirely, suggesting GPT 5.6 has a broader, albeit imperfect, application scope in sensitive domains. In "hidden animal" tests, GPT 5.6 failed to correctly identify a camouflaged frog and partially misidentified a hidden toad, indicating that its visual perception, while strong, still lags behind Claude Fable 5 in certain nuanced recognition tasks.

For deep research and data synthesis, GPT 5.6 proved exceptionally capable. It generated a comprehensive and concise report on the molecular drivers of a specific type of leukemia, complete with relevant tables, flowcharts, citations, and sections on targeted therapy and resistance mechanisms. Furthermore, utilizing the new "Work" tab in ChatGPT, the model autonomously fetched Q1 2026 earnings reports for Alphabet, Nvidia, and Amazon, synthesizing the data into a professional presentation comparing their financials and future outlooks, offering insightful conclusions.

In terms of performance benchmarks and competitive analysis, GPT 5.6 Soul consistently demonstrated leading capabilities. On the "Agent's Last Exam" benchmark, which assesses long-horizon professional tasks, GPT 5.6 Soul achieved the highest score at a significantly lower cost compared to Claude Opus and Claude Fable. Similarly, in agentic coding benchmarks, GPT 5.6 Soul outperformed Claude Fable while maintaining superior cost-efficiency. For genomics tasks (Genebench), GPT 5.6 Soul significantly surpassed Claude Opus, with Claude Fable notably absent due to its strict guardrails against biology-related queries.

OpenAI also revealed that GPT 5.6 is actively used internally to accelerate its own research and development, highlighting a "recursive R&D loop" where current AI models aid in developing future generations. While independent leaderboards like Artificial Analysis show GPT 5.6 Soul Max slightly behind Claude Fable 5 in overall performance, it is considerably more cost-efficient. An important metric, the Omniscience Hallucination Rate, indicated GPT 5.6 Soul Max at 89% for specific benchmark questions, which is higher than Claude Fable (55%) and GLM 5.2 (28%), requiring careful consideration in critical applications.

However, on the Deep Sweet leaderboard for long-horizon software engineering tasks, GPT 5.6 Soul Max edged out Claude Fable 5, demonstrating greater efficiency with lower average cost and output tokens. Furthermore, in ARC AGI 2 and ARC AGI 3 benchmarks, which test an AI's ability to learn new patterns and solve visual puzzles on the fly, GPT 5.6 Soul achieved remarkably high scores (92.5% for ARC AGI 2 and nearly 8% for ARC AGI 3), far surpassing other frontier models and showcasing a strong emergent learning capability. AbacusAI's Livebench also positioned GPT 5.6 Soul as a leader in reasoning, agentic coding, mathematics, and language.

GPT 5.6 is progressively rolling out. Paid users of the online ChatGPT platform gain access to GPT 5.6 Soul, while the ChatGPT desktop app (Codeex) offers GPT 5.6 Terra to free users and all three models (Soul, Terra, Luna) with adjustable effort levels to paid subscribers. The model is also available via API.

In conclusion, GPT 5.6 represents a significant advancement in AI, particularly for agentic applications requiring autonomous, multi-step problem-solving. Its impressive performance across various complex tasks, coupled with its cost-efficiency, positions it as one of the leading models available. While some limitations in visual content generation accuracy and a higher hallucination rate on specific benchmarks exist, its emergent learning capabilities and robust agentic framework mark a pivotal step forward in AI development.
